A seat is an imprint filed at the national library. The applicant gives an ISSN, an address, and ISBNs spent; the node reads the legal deposit register and wants two copies of each title in sixty days. One imprint, one seat. A sonnet sequence is one title whether or not it sells, a comet of a first-week bestseller leaves no slip, a hollow catalogue on deposit scores nothing.

Deposit carries the cost: 1,200 dollars to print 300 copies, twelve titles a year, 15,000 a clone yearly. Fifty clones burn 750,000 keeping shelves, since a spine can be pulled and read but an empty slot cannot.
